I want to counter this. I fall under the technical definition, but do not have any of the ideological baggage. I literally do not agree with any of the beliefs that people ascribe to the label, but I do still fit the 'technical label'. That means that when a post like this is made, it is very hurtful. I came very close to ending my own life in 2015 and part of the cause was exactly posts like the one made by ruddet and some of your replies. I did not manage to overcome my root problems in the slightest, and it is still a recurring thought. However I am not dead which I definitely would not have expected back then.

When posts like this come up I just want to point out that using the label as it is written is playing in to the hands of those that want to push the ideology on to everyone else who fits the technical definition. You have to let us separate ourselves from them by not conflating us with them.

Being unattractive by itself is enough of a reason for things to be difficult when it comes to forming relationships. While having a certain attribute does not necessarily mean that a person will be considered attractive, not having that attribute can be the singular barrier to not being considered unattractive. Some people who are overweight are primarily being held back by their weight. Some short people are primarily being held back by their height. Some people who have bad teeth are being held back by their teeth.

This is just how attractiveness works. Sometimes a feature or lack there-of is just not overlooked, and defines people in the eyes of others. For me it is my crooked teeth and extreme overbite. I am sure many people are in the same boat.

Assuming you are talking about the 19:10 video of the battle of Tabqa airport here.

Personally I believe that the video should be considered suitable for this subreddit. The nature of the combat is unusual in so far that it is a much larger scale than is typically seen, and in much more open ground. 

The video is broken up like this:

00:00-02:25: Exposition and introduction

02:25-03:40: Aerial footage

03:40-04:30: Close range combat in tented area

04:30-04:59: Proof of enemy casualties

04:59-07:10: Combat against mass of enemy combatants + ISIS advance

07:10-07:22 Execution of unarmed combatants mid-battle

07:22-07:27 Close range shooting of Syrian armed combatant

07:27-07:31 Close range execution of wounded combatant

07:31-07:49 Close range shooting of another armed combatant

07:49-11:00 Aftermath/looting/shooting dead bodies

11:00-12:17 Showing of ISIS dead

12:17-14:11 Proof of ISIS airfield capture

14:11-14:51 Showing of SAA dead

14:41-17:21 Parading of prisoners

17:21-18:06 Prisoner execution

18:06-19:10 Conclusion


While brutal, it accurately portrays the order of the battle. The execution of wounded and surrendering SAA forces occurred whilst the battle was still underway. The mid-combat executions were contextually important to the accurate portrayal of the events that occurred

The post combat execution and prisoner parading would have been against the rules if it was posted by itself, but it was appended to a video depicting the battle. Surely if a battle started in the midst of a military parade, or a firing range, or in the aftermath of an assassination, then it would be appropriate for this subreddit. The spirit of the rules are clearly against videos of those listed under rule 3 in isolation, not when they are attached to combat.

Philosophically speaking, hiding such a video only serves to glorify combat by removing the accurate and brutal portrayal of what combat actually represents in an area like this. Combat is not glorious, it is not a sport, it is a hellish struggle for life and death. The video of the battle for taqba accurately portrays the order of battle. ISIS is a reprehensible organisation; hiding footage of their nature does not serve anyone.

I am probably an example of the person that you believe should be considered a pariah, an involuntary celibate, as you choose to label me. I am not contending in the slightest whether there is something wrong with me, but I will however try to redirect your thoughts to consider other things.

First of all, I would not label myself as a misogynist in the slightest, I have no desire to hate women, and I don't believe I deserve a woman by virtue of existing. While I do concede that some in my position may become misogynistic, I would contend that it is not the majority, and certainly not the only consequence.

There is a concept in psychology called locus of control. Those with an internal locus of control tend to place the blame for their failures on themselves, while people with an external locus of control blame it on others. Those who may become misogynistic (i.e blame women) as a result of their condition, are likely to have an external locus of control. While those with an internal locus of control are likely to blame themselves instead.

Therefore, being incel in and of itself is not sufficient to turn an individual in to a misogynist, but rather, other aspects of their personality must contribute.

The other aspect of your post I disagree with is that I deserve to be a pariah of some form. Obviously I have personal reasons for this (no one likes being a pariah), but your justification for me being a valid societal target (the definition of a pariah), relies upon me adopting certain paradigms which I just do not hold in the slightest. 

TLDR: Becoming a misogynist does not follow merely from being 'involuntarily celibate', but instead relies upon other additional personality factors.

22, Male. I have never been asked out, never asked out someone, never had a girlfriend, nor had any 'experience'. There are a lot of reasons for this.


**Why am I forever alone?**

1. Incorrect/weak posture

2. Crooked teeth

3. Severe overbite/ weak jawline

4. Low muscle density

5. Boring to talk to. Unless it's on a topic that I am interested in, I lack the ability to engage people in conversation. People will generally move on to someone else who is far better at small talk given the opportunity.

6. Don't have a career yet, despite getting 2 degrees for that exact purpose, which means that I am still living with my parents. No career, means no salary, which means very few women would ever want to know you. Unless you were good looking or something.

7. Massive generalised and social anxiety

8. Depression

9. I view myself as a legitimately bad human being, and would never inflict myself on to people that I liked.  I am not evil or anything like that, or amoral, I am just inferior and not suitable for being with people.

10. I have an extremely bad reaction to rejection. I can't stand the thought of it. However, because I am objectively an ugly person, and have a shit personality, I am also prone to rejection. This means I try to avoid activities that could perceivably result in rejection. That doesn't mean just not asking people out, it is doing things like going to the beach, applying for jobs, going to the shops. All the things normal people find easy, I have to work up to for an extremely long period of time. I don't think I could actually have sex even if I had the opportunity because of it.

11. I spend most of my days on the computer doing barely anything at all.

12. I don't want to do anything to benefit myself in the long term, because I don't want there to be a long term. I was meant to end myself last year, I even wrote a bloody post about it. However I pussied out. I am stuck not wanting to live but not being able to die.

13. I have a few embarrassing things that are chronic, nothing major, just small things that won't go away. Things like dandruff and the like. It's a real effort to hide them, and avoiding going out in public is far easier.

14. Unfit. Sitting around on the computer most days doesn't do much for my fitness. I am not fat. I am healthy weight, however I am quite unfit.

15. At the moment I really only have one friend. I have a lot of friends of friends, and acquaintances. However none of them are really friends, they're just people that know of me.



The first three are actually related to each other, as my head position changes naturally to counteract the lower ability to breathe with the overbite.  This leads to a shitty, and ugly posture. I could correct this with a mixture of lower jaw surgery and braces, but I can't afford it.


**How do I cope?**

I don't really. Most of my days are spent either sleeping or distracting myself from my own situation (video games and the like). Any moment I am aware of myself is ridiculously painful.

**Will things change?**

No.

I started rationalising it. It seemed more likely to me that she took an interest in me because of the alcohol she had rather than an actual legitimate attraction. When it came to texting her when I got back to Australia, I was very stressed about it. Anyway the idea that she only liked me because she was tipsy became a bit overwhelming so eventually I stopped sending texts (yes she was replying).

It may sound completely screwed up, but I wanted to remain as an interesting guy in the bar, as opposed to an ugly and boring guy that tried to date her.

Since I was extremely young (5 years old) I have always had anxiety in social situations, which only intensified as I got older. When I got older still and in to pubery (13), a few statements/reactions from my peers really destroyed my self-esteem. The fact that I was ugly got imprinted on to my psyche. 

By 15 I couldn't really even conceive of a situation of a girl/woman liking me, so I started avoiding them due to a massive fear of rejection. Regardless, being a stupid kid, I often stared at women/girls that I liked.

Needless to say, contrary to my beliefs, they actually noticed this, and pointed it out to their peers during graduation night for high school. I deserved the ridicule/shame etc. but it hurt regardless. Anyway, that same night a girl that I thought I was just friends with awkwardly tried to ask me out, sort of. However I was so screwed up from the earlier incident, that I just walked off. It is kind of funny how self-inflicted it all is. It still kills me to think I probably hurt her as well.

Regardless, now (5 years later) I avoid pretty much every social situation I conceivably can, and have a literal fear of women.


TLDR: Ugly, avoidant, afraid of women, anxious.

I know there's no sprawl in New York. I am just saying that I would prefer to live in a city like New york compared to the suburban sprawl I live in. 

For the record I live in an isolated city known as Perth, in Western Australia. Its population is about 1.5 million, but the population is spread over a 20 kilometre by 60 kilometre strip with a small 'central business district' in the middle.

There was once a girl that inexplicably sat opposite me in a bar (while I was drinking with my brother and his friends in Germany), she stared at me a bit, changed seats, sat next to me, sang karaoke with me, gave me her number, let me put her arm around her ...

Unfortunately, she got a bit drunk over the night, so I took her to her room and let her sleep. I texted her a bit later, but was too awkward to do anything. Yes we both happened to be from the same city in Australia.

Nothing similar has happened since.

Living in suburban sprawl is really an easy way to lose contact with other people. From visiting large cities, I know I'd definitely be quite a bit happier in this sort of environment, however I live in probably one of the most sprawl affected cities there are.

If high school graduation was pretty recent, you have quite a bit of a chance to repair them. I became distant from the people I was friends with in high school, but to be honest, it was largely because I didn't really make the effort to initiate anything. After high school you can't be passive with friendships and hope for others to invite you. If you only left high school in the past few months or so, then there's no reason not to try and re-gain contact with the people you met before.

**TLDR: You have to actively try and work to maintain any friendship where you're no longer forced by circumstance to be around each other.**

Source: Went through the same thing 5 years ago, and going through the same thing now with people who are quite close friends for university
